newsitem.title: USA: Rain to spread through U.S. Midwest next two days.
newsitem.headline: Rain to spread through U.S. Midwest next two days.

text.p: A cold front entering the central U.S. from the north should bring 0.5 to 2.0 inches of rain Tuesday in the northern and western Midwest before moving east Wednesday into Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio, meteorologists said.
"The heaviest (rain) activity would tend to favor the northern areas the next 36 hours or so," said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp meteorologist.
Wednesday's showers should produce 0.50 to 1.50 inches of rainfall with 70 percent coverage from eastern Iowa to Ohio.

However, Burgio said the heaviest rain may again miss a dry area in central Illinois bordered by Peoria, Decatur and Springfield. He said storm systems this season have tracked north or south of that area leaving it short of moisture.
June rainfall for Springfield, Ill., was 1.54 inches versus the normal of 3.43, said Burgio.
After Wednesday, the Midwest should be mostly dry and cool, with the next chance for significant rain July 7 and 8, said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Corp.
After Tuesday's highs in the lows 90-degrees Fahrenheit area, temperatures should range in the 70s to low 80s through the weekend for much of the Midwest.
"The heat stays west. It doesn't really get much further east than Des Moines," said Gesser of 90-plus temperatures later this week.
